cards.text: Baker, these are the words of a man named Amos, and what he saw concerns Israel. It came two years before the earthquake, when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel. So who is this guy?

cards.question: Amos is about to carry the LORD's words. Amos was among the ___ of Tekoa.

cards.text: A sheepherder from Tekoa, and I'm a cookie stamper who did years in a junk drawer, so who am I to judge a résumé? Then Amos says the LORD roars from Zion, and friend, that is not a whisper, that is a ROAR.

cards.question: True or false: when the LORD roars from Zion, the pastures of the shepherds rejoice.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks, and He starts with Damascus, the head of Aram (Isaiah 7:8). He says, "For three transgressions of Damascus, even four, I will not revoke My judgment," and He's got more to say.

cards.question: The LORD says He will not revoke His judgment on Damascus. What does that mean?
The LORD gives His reason for judging Damascus. What did Damascus do to Gilead?

answers.text: Threshed Gilead with sledges of iron
Starved Gilead with a long siege
Cut down Gilead's forests with axes

cards.question: The LORD names the house of Hazael and Ben-hadad, kings of Aram (2 Kings 13:3, 24). He says He will send ___ upon the house of Hazael to consume the citadels of Ben-hadad.

cards.text: Then He gets specific: He will break down the gates of Damascus and cut off the rulers in the Valley of Aven and Beth-eden. I once gave a baker directions by pointing my mustache and saying "over there," and friend, the LORD does not do "over there."

cards.question: True or false: the LORD says that after He breaks down the gates of Damascus, the people of Aram will get to stay in their land.

cards.text: Next up is Gaza, a Philistine city (Joshua 13:3), and there's that line again: three transgressions, even four, and no taking back the judgment. Hear it twice and you know it like the beep of your own oven timer.

cards.question: The LORD gives His charge against Gaza. What does He say Gaza did to a whole population?

answers.text: Exiled them and handed them to Edom
Drove them out into the desert
Burned their homes to the ground

cards.text: So the LORD will send fire upon the walls of Gaza. Then He names Ashdod, Ashkelon and Ekron, like a whole group chat getting called out one name at a time.

cards.question: True or false: after Ashdod, Ashkelon and Ekron, the LORD says whoever is left of the Philistines will be spared.

cards.text: Next is Tyre, a fortified city (Joshua 19:29), and Tyre also delivered up a whole congregation of exiles to Edom. But Tyre's charge has one more piece.

cards.question: Besides handing exiles over to Edom, what else does the LORD charge Tyre with?

cards.text: So the LORD will send fire upon the walls of Tyre to consume its citadels. Three nations in, and nobody's walked away clean.

Next on the list is Edom, and Esau, Jacob's twin brother, is the father of the Edomites (Genesis 25:24-26; 36:9). And there's that line again, three transgressions, even four, so by now you could say it right along with Him.

cards.question: Edom's charge sounds personal. What does the LORD say Edom did?

answers.text: Pursued his brother with the sword

cards.question: True or false: the LORD says Edom's anger flared up once and then cooled off.

cards.text: So the LORD will send fire upon Teman to consume the citadels of Bozrah. Teman, Bozrah, friend, I need a map just to keep up, and I live on a planet barely big enough for my bakery.
Then come the Ammonites, descended from Lot, Abraham's nephew (Genesis 12:5; 19:36, 38). What they did is hard to even say out loud: they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead.

cards.question: The Ammonites ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead. What does the LORD say they did it for?

cards.text: So the LORD will kindle a fire in the walls of Rabbah, the Ammonite city (2 Samuel 12:26). War cries on the day of battle, a violent wind on the day of tempest, friend, Rabbah is getting the WHOLE forecast.

cards.question: The LORD says the Ammonite king will go into ___, he and his princes together.

cards.text: Next up is Moab, also descended from Lot (Genesis 19:36-37). Five nations down, and friend, I am on the very edge of my gold base waiting on this next charge.

cards.question: Moab's charge has to do with the king of Edom, another nation's ruler. True or false: the LORD holds Moab responsible for it.
What does the LORD say Moab did to the king of Edom?

answers.text: Took his crown as a prize

cards.text: So the LORD will send fire against Moab, on the citadels of Kerioth. Moab will die in tumult, with war cries and the sound of the ram's horn, and friend, that horn is NOT playing elevator music.

cards.question: True or false: the LORD says only the ruler of Moab will be cut off, and his officials will be spared.

cards.text: And now the list comes home: the next name is Judah, where Amos's own town of Tekoa sits (2 Chronicles 11:5-6). It's like nodding along in a meeting while everybody else gets called out, and then the boss says YOUR name.

cards.question: The LORD's charge against Judah is that they reject the ___ of the LORD and fail to keep His statutes.

cards.text: Did you catch that, friend? Six nations got called out for what they did to people, and Judah gets called out for what it did with the Law of the LORD, a WHOLE different charge.

cards.question: Judah is led astray by the lies their fathers walked in. What does that say about Judah's problem?

cards.text: So Judah gets the same sentence as the nations: fire upon Judah to consume the citadels of Jerusalem. Same fire, friend, and not one name on this list gets a pass.

findings.problem: Most of this stop's choices require luck rather than reasoning. Cards 2, 7, 8, 12 and 16 ask for Amos's occupation, Damascus's charge, the judgment on Hazael's house, Gaza's charge or Tyre's additional charge without earlier cards giving any basis for inferring the answer. These five cards alone make a majority of the stop's nine choices discovery questions.

rule.text: Could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Nothing in the opening card lets the baker infer Amos's occupation. The blank therefore asks for the unseen wording "sheepherders," not a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: No earlier card has introduced fire as the judgment, so the baker can only guess the unseen word "fire" in the line about the house of Hazael.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Most of this stop's choices also depend on luck. Cards 2, 3, 6, 8 and 11 ask for Edom's action, the duration of Edom's anger, the Ammonites' purpose, the Ammonite king's destination or Moab's action without enough earlier context to reason out any of them. That is a majority of the stop's nine choices, rather than a few discovery questions.

A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The preceding card mentions fire, battle and a violent wind, but gives no basis for inferring that the Ammonite king will go into "exile." The blank asks the baker to guess the next word of the line.

findings.problem: This story card only reviews the six preceding charges and repeats Judah's already-answered charge concerning the Law. It does not move the baker forward through the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
